subject: Post-demo: SLO gap analysis & proposed reliability tests
messages:
From: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@brightpay.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from demo — reliability & SLO questions

Alex — thanks again for the demo today, it helped illustrate Redwood's latency profile. We took notes and the SRE team flagged a few items we need to validate before we can progress: 

- Target uptime we need: 99.95% per month (regional). Can Redwood provide historical availability for equivalent production clusters or an SLA commit?
- Rate limiting/burst behavior: how are customer-level rate limits enforced across Dedicated vs Hosted? We need to simulate bursts on payday windows (short, high QPS) and understand throttling/failure modes.
- Error budget handling & visibility: if we cross our error budget, what automated fallbacks exist (e.g., smaller model, cached responses) and how are these surfaced in logs/alerts?
- Failover behavior: for multi-region accounts, how does traffic fail over? Is there automatic model variant fallback when a GPU pool is degraded?
- KV/prefix cache semantics: for our payroll prompts we rely on prefix caching to keep median latency low — how long is KV preserved across requests from the same customer ID?
- Observability artifacts: we need request-level traces and token-level latency histograms for our audit.

Attached: BrightPay-SRE-questions.xlsx (spreadsheet with granular QA items).

Our timeline: we'd like a short plan and a proposed test schedule by next Tue (21 Jul). Can you propose a minimal set of tests that would validate the items above and who from Redwood will own them?

Thanks,
Sarah Connors
Head of Platform Reliability
BrightPay

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@brightpay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — reliability & SLO questions

Sarah — really appreciate the clear list. I've read the attached spreadsheet and sketched a short validation plan below (high level), plus where we'll need help from BrightPay to run realistic load. See attached SLO-matrix-redwood.csv and redwood-test-plan.pdf for details.

Proposed minimal validation tests (what we'll run / what you can run):
1) Availability baseline: run a 72-hr smoke on our Hosted endpoint with representative traffic (we'll provide a replay harness). We'll provide uptime and incident traces for that window and a 30-day rolling availability summary from comparable customers.
2) Burst QPS experiments: simulate 5x and 10x payday bursts for 30m windows against a Dedicated pool and Hosted. We'll measure tail latency, token-drop ratio, and token throttle responses.
3) Failover & variant fallback: induce a simulated GPU pool degradation and verify automatic model fallback to pinned lower-capacity variant (configurable). Verify request continuity and degradation profile.
4) Error-budget policies: step failure injection at 0.5%/1%/2% to see alerting thresholds and automated fallback triggers.
5) Cache retention validation: run a sequence of prefix-heavy requests (customer cookie) and observe KV hit rate across 1h/6h/24h windows.

Ownership & timeline:
- Redwood test harness + initial runs: Alex Martinez (owner) — target start 07/20; preliminary data 07/22.
- Rate-limit & stress profiles: Karthik Iyer (infra lead) — will provide rate-limit configs and simulated client harness.
- Observability & artifacts (traces/histograms): Monica Patel (console/telemetry) — will ensure request-level exports and sample dashboards.

What we need from BrightPay to make tests meaningful:
- Representative request traces or sample prompt templates (anonymized)
- Expected concurrency profile for pay cycles (QPS/time series)
- A whitelist of any external integrations to avoid during tests

I can walk through the redwood-test-plan.pdf in a short working call; otherwise we'll start with the 72-hr baseline and the burst sims.

Attachments: SLO-matrix-redwood.csv (SLO coverage and proposed SLA language), redwood-test-plan.pdf (detailed runbook), perf-harness-config.yaml (client config stub).

Best,
Alex Martinez
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
alex_martinez@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0149

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: BrightPay validation — action items & owners

Quick internal runbook based on Sarah's ask and my reply. We need to be surgical — BrightPay expects results next Tue (21 Jul) but we can ask for 24–48h slack if needed.

Action items (owners):
- Karthik: prepare rate-limit configs and the client harness. Two scenarios: (A) Hosted throttling behavior; (B) Dedicated pool saturating (simulate shard eviction). Deliverable: perf-harness-config.yaml, two test scripts. Target: start 07/20 EOD, run 07/21/07/22.
- Monica: wire up trace exports for the test runs and pre-bake a dashboard with token-latency percentiles, token-drop events, and per-request model-variant info. Deliverable: shared dashboard link + JSON. Target: dashboard ready 07/21 morning.
- Alex (me): coordinate with BrightPay for sample prompts and the replay harness; run the 72-hr baseline on Hosted starting 07/20 21:00 UTC. Collect 72-hr artifact and produce a one-page summary.
- Marissa: brief (optional) — prepare a one-paragraph summary for the account execs if BrightPay pushes contract questions after tests.

Risks & notes:
- We'll need a short IP/PII-safe scrub step for any traces BrightPay shares (Monica).
- Failover test will require discretionary capacity — confirm with infra (Karthik) before forcing degradation on customer-like pools.

I will keep Sarah in the loop once we have the first run results. If any blocking infra needs support, flag here and I'll escalate.

Alex

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Internal: BrightPay validation — action items & owners

Thanks — scheduling looks good. A couple of technical clarifications before we start: 

1) Hosted throttling: we'll exercise the rate limiter at the token-dispatch layer (per-customer token window). I will produce two config variants — one that returns 429s and one that queues with progressive backpressure so we can measure both failure and latency-based degradation.
2) Dedicated pool saturation: we'll simulate a noisy-neighbor on a single GPU host and then trigger our fallback policy (model variant pin to smaller quantized model). I will document exact CPU/GPU metrics to capture.
3) Observability: Monica — I'll emit a short-lived tracing header so you can stitch requests end-to-end across the fallback events.

I'll upload the harness and the config files to the shared Drive folder this afternoon (perf-harness-config.yaml + scripts).

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
